dimensions.assessment: Affects federal employees covered by collective bargaining agreements under chapter 71 of title 5, United States Code, federal agencies, and labor unions.
dimensions.evidence: terminate any provision of a collective bargaining agreement entered into under this chapter that is in force and effect

dimensions.assessment: Alters the terms of existing labor agreements and federal workplace rules for federal employees when exercised by an incoming President.
dimensions.evidence: A provision of any collective bargaining agreement that conflicts with a rule, executive order... shall not be enforceable.

dimensions.assessment: The source text does not state or imply direct federal spending or revenue changes.
Amends chapter 71 of title 5, United States Code, to add presidential authority regarding federal labor agreements.
dimensions.evidence: To amend chapter 71 of title 5, United States Code, to provide the President discretion to negotiate collective bargaining agreements

dimensions.assessment: Permanently amends the statutory authorities available to future U.S. Presidents concerning federal labor agreements.
dimensions.evidence: The authority under subsection (a) may not be exercised by an incumbent President.

missing_information: Specific economic or fiscal estimates related to altering federal collective bargaining agreements.
importance_detail.rationale: This bill grants incoming U.S. Presidents the discretion to terminate existing collective bargaining agreement provisions for federal agency employees upon taking office and clarifies that conflicting presidential orders render such provisions unenforceable.
